name: Personal Learning and Development (L&D Tracker)
procedure: a. Define what you would like to achieve and the motivation to pursue it
b. Discuss and evaluate the required skills to achieve your desired outcome
c. Inventory the target skill(s) and assess your current knowledge/application of each skill
d. Prioritize skills and select skill for development
e. Evaluate and select appropriate training within quarter to support desired outcome
f. Complete training and write Knowledge Sharing 1 Pager
g. Present 1 Pager and save to Knowledge Wiki
h. Compare desired outcome to actual outcome and return to step d to continue to pursue desired outcome.
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Team Learning and Development (L&D Tracker)
procedure: a. Define what you would like to achieve and the motivation to pursue it
b. Discuss and evaluate the required skills to achieve your desired outcome
c. Inventory the target skill(s) and assess your current knowledge/application of each skill
d. Prioritize skills and select skill for development
e. Evaluate and select appropriate team training within quarter to support desired outcome
f. Complete training and write Facilitate Team Retrospective
g. Create Knowledge Wiki
h. Compare desired outcome to actual outcome and return to step d to continue to pursue desired outcome.
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Company Compliance Training (L&D Tracker)
procedure: a. Track Company Compliance Training requirements in KNET, KNET2, and FastCap
b. Complete training

name: Document Review
procedure: a. Receive Document (PRFAQ, MBR, 6 Pager)
b. Schedule time to review and provide written feedback
c. Review Document and Document Feedback
d. Communicate feedback (live, email, chime)
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Team Introductions and Engagements
procedure: a. Identify new partner team or PXT stakeholder
b. Communicate interest for introduction and engagement
c. Schedule Team Intro/Engagement Communication Cycle
d. Review Team PRFAQs, MBRs, 6 Pagers, Wikis, and Data
e. Discuss synergies for process improvement
f. Coordinate intake of process improvement opportunities
trigger: First working day of month

name: Innovation Process - Explore Opportunities
procedure: a.     	Add new Opportunity Name to row in Opportunity Tracker
b. Provide a brief 1-2 sentence Opportunity Description of the opportunity.
c. Select the Strategic Category for the opportunity
d. Identify the Executive Sponsor for the opportunity
e. Select the Desired Timeframe for the opportunity to be implemented
f. Identify the Owner/Driver for the opportunity (the person completing opportunity deliverables)
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Innovation Process - Evaluate Opportunity
procedure: a. Document Target 3-7 Use Cases related to opportunity.  Use cases are based on activities in a process and specific scenarios encountered.
b. Document the technologies proposed for this opportunity
c. Define the primary customer impacted by the opportunity
d. Document the flow of activities / steps in the process from start to finish
e. Estimate opportunity benefit (target population with time, cost, quality benefits)
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - PRFAQ
procedure: a. Update the Opportunity Status field to Active - PRFAQ
b. Complete Writing Hub - Writing Like an Companyian (one time training)
c.      	Reference Writing Hub PRFAQ Site for Template and Instructions
d.     	Create a PRFAQ document based on PRFAQ Template
i. Who is the customer?
ii. What is the problem or opportunity we propose to solve?
iii. What is the most important customer benefit?
iv. What does the customer experience look like?
v. How do you know what customers need or want?
vi. Identify the Business Case & Target Use Case(s)
vii. Outline Technology Model - Add Link to Opportunity Tracker
viii. Diagram the Customer Experience Workflow
ix. Complete Frequently Asked Questions Template
x. Complete Press Release 1 Pager
c. Submit for Steering Committee PRFAQ Review & Proof of Concept Greenlight
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Proof of Concept/Prototype
procedure: a. Complete Prototype Plan based on Prototype Plan Template
i. Purpose of Prototype
ii. Scope of Prototype
iii. Prototype Features (e.g., platform, targeted use cases, front end, backend)
iv. User Experience Workflow
v. Success Criteria
vi. Future Use Cases
b. Build Prototype to Success Criteria
i. Prototype - Instructions for use
ii. Prototype Test Results
iii. Lessons Learned and Product Assessment
c. Outline Implementation/Development Plan with Resource Type and FTE Requirements for implementation
d. Estimate Annualized Net Benefit if Opportunity implemented
e. Identify possible Risks to completing opportunity implementation and create Mitigation Plan for each risk
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Product Assessment
procedure: 4. Complete Product Assessment Document based on Product Assessment Template
a. Business Scope
b. Technical Scope
c. Prototype Target Use Cases
d. Prototype Success Criteria and Test Results
e. Product Use Cases with Annualized Net Benefit
f. Product Risks and Mitigation Plan
g. Product Stakeholders
h. Assumptions
i. Constraints
j. Dependencies
k. User Experience Workflows
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Initiate New Product/Program
procedure: 5. Cultivate Opportunity with internal/external stakeholders and executive committee approval
a. Update Opportunity Discovery fields (section 3) as needed
b. Update the Weekly Status field
c. Update Opportunity Stage as required opportunity fields are finalized
d. Finalize the Implementation Requirements based on prioritized business requirements and technical model
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: PDCA Cycle
procedure: a. Determine a target activity or process area of interest, the "theme" for the activity and a baseline current condition measurement of the activity.
B. Establish a future state target condition measurement for the activity.
C. Propose an experiment or improvement that can be worked on over the next 48 hours.
D. Spend 10-60 minutes working on the proposed experiment/improvement.
E. Meet every 48 hours to measure the current condition and document results of your experiment.

F. If current condition meets target condition for 3 meetings, select a new process area for improvement. if current condition does not meet target condition go to step D. and propose a new experiment.
trigger: Prior PDCA cycle measurement recorded

name: 6S Email Activity
procedure: 1. When number of inbox emails exceeds 20, identify:
a. Immediate Action
b. Planned Action/Keep Emails
i. Save to Task/Project Email Folder
ii. Archive
c. Delete Emails
2. When any email exceeds 90 days, identify:
a. Any action to be taken
b. Save to Task/Project Email Folder
c. Archive
d. Delete
3. Set Rules and Alerts in Microsoft Office
1. If you are creating a rule to move messages to another folder, make sure that you have created the folder before you start to create the rule using File, New, Folder.
2. Find the message that you want to base the rule on in Outlook and select it so that it is highlighted.
3. Click on the Organize button. You will find this on the top taskbar - it is a yellow button made up of lots of squares, or in the Tools menu.
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: High-value Communication Time-blocking (30-60 minutes)
trigger: Same time each work day

name: High-value team and project meetings (15-30 minutes)
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Connecting with other Companyians (15-60 minutes)
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Document Writing (Backlog, Updates, Blurbs, Narratives)
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Refining Program Plan
procedure: a. Open current Program Plan and latest sprint outcomes.
b. Identify gaps: slipped milestones, changed scope, new dependencies, resource shifts.
c. Incorporate stakeholder feedback from last week's 1:1s and reviews.
d. Update milestone dates, owners, and dependency links.
e. Note the diff in a short changelog block.
f. Publish updated plan to team channel.
trigger: Mid-Sprint Review (Fri Wk1) OR program-plan-drift signal

name: DMAIC Project Charter
procedure: a. Write the problem statement in one paragraph.
b. Document the business case (current cost / risk, expected benefit).
c. Define in-scope and out-of-scope process boundaries.
d. Identify Process Owner, Sponsor, Project Lead, and team members.
e. Set goal statement: baseline X → target Y by date Z.
f. Estimate sprint count (typical DMAIC: 6–8 sprints).
g. Identify top 3 risks and initial mitigations.
h. Obtain Sponsor signature.
i. Register Charter in project portfolio.
trigger: Decision to launch a DMAIC project after Kaizen / variance analysis

name: DMAIC SIPOC
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Output Data Collection Plan
procedure: a. List CTQ output metrics (Y's) from VOC/VOB/VOA.
b. For each metric document: operational definition, unit, method, sampling plan, owner, tool, storage.
c. If measurement risk exists, run MSA (#31) before locking.
d. Pilot DCP for one cycle.
e. Lock DCP and proceed to Baseline (#28).
trigger: Post-SIPOC, before Baseline (#28)

name: DMAIC Stakeholder Analysis
procedure: a. List all stakeholders impacted by or influencing the project.
b. For each, rate Influence (H/M/L) and Interest (H/M/L).
c. Plot on 2x2 grid; assign quadrant engagement approach.
d. Assign owner per quadrant.
e. Document in Stakeholder Analysis template; feed into Communication Plan.
trigger: DMAIC Charter signed

name: DMAIC Communication Plan
procedure: a. Copy the four Stakeholder Analysis quadrants into the Comm Plan matrix.
b. For each row define cadence, channel, format, owner.
c. Write an acceptance criterion per row.
d. Book recurring calendar holds for every synchronous touchpoint.
e. Publish and revisit at each Sprint Retrospective.
trigger: Stakeholder Analysis complete

name: DMAIC Risk and Mitigation Plan
procedure: a. Brainstorm risks in four buckets: technical, organizational, timeline, resource.
b. For each risk rate Probability (1–5) × Impact (1–5).
c. For score ≥ 12 write a mitigation plan and assign a risk owner.
d. For score 6–11 write a monitoring plan.
e. Record in Risk Register template.
f. Review at every Sprint Retrospective.
trigger: Post-Charter; refresh at each Sprint Retrospective

name: DMAIC VOC/VOB/VOA Analysis
procedure: a. Voice of Customer: interview 3–5 customers.
b. Voice of Business: interview 2–3 business leaders.
c. Voice of Associate: interview 3–5 associates.
d. Translate each raw voice into a CTQ requirement.
e. Prioritize CTQs by frequency, severity, strategic fit.
f. Document and feed into Output DCP (#22) and C&E Matrix (#34).
trigger: Post-Charter

outputArtifact.name: VOC / VOB / VOA Document with CTQs

name: DMAIC Continuous Reporting Framework
procedure: a. Define reporting cadence (weekly or monthly).
b. Select metrics: baseline, current, target, delta, trend, sigma, financial.
c. Build dashboard linked to DCP data source.
d. Assign owner and monthly review slot.
e. Publish link per Communication Plan (#24).
trigger: Post-Baseline (#28)

name: DMAIC Baseline Output Performance Data
procedure: a. Execute DCP for baseline period (30 working days or 30 samples).
b. Collect data per plan; log deviations.
c. If manual measurement, verify with MSA (#31).
d. Compute summary statistics: n, mean, median, stdev, min, max, Cp/Cpk, sigma.
e. Build baseline Control Chart (#29).
f. Record baseline value in Charter as locked reference.
trigger: Output DCP locked

name: DMAIC Control Chart Graph
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Process Capability Report
procedure: a. Verify data normality (histogram + Anderson-Darling).
b. Define spec limits (USL / LSL).
c. Calculate short-term capability: Cp, Cpk.
d. Calculate long-term performance: Pp, Ppk.
e. Compute DPMO and process sigma.
f. Flag if Cpk < 1.33.
trigger: Baseline data locked

name: DMAIC MSA Report
procedure: a. Select 10 samples covering the expected process range.
b. 2–3 appraisers measure each sample 2–3 times randomized.
c. Compute Gage R&R (repeatability + reproducibility).
d. Acceptance: <10% excellent; 10–30% marginal; >30% unacceptable.
e. If unacceptable, fix and re-run MSA.
f. Document results and decision.
trigger: Output DCP drafted; before locking

name: DMAIC Detailed Process Maps
procedure: 1. Complete high level process map (SIPOC)
2. Detail 3-7 key sub-processes
3. Estimate process times and wait times
4. Define the inputs and outputs for each step
5. Identify all steps in the process as value added and non-value added
6. Identify 1-3 relevant measurement opportunities for each sub-process
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Quick Win Improvements
procedure: a. Filter: lead < 1 week AND cost < $1K AND effort < 2 pd AND reversible.
b. Get Process Owner approval.
c. Implement change.
d. Measure impact before and after (≥ 5 observations each).
e. Log: name, hypothesis, delta, decision.
f. Feed kept wins into Improvement Backlog (#38).
trigger: Quick-win candidate identified (lead < 1w, cost < $1K, effort < 2 person-days)

name: DMAIC Cause and Effect Matrix/Analysis
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Inputs Data Collection Plan
procedure: a. Take top-scored X variables from C&E Matrix (4–6 inputs).
b. For each X document: operational definition, method, sampling plan, owner, tool.
c. For each X-Y pair confirm the time-stamp join key.
d. If any X is subjective/manual, run MSA (#31) for that X.
e. Pilot for one cycle; fix and re-pilot if n < 80%.
f. Lock the Input DCP.
g. Execute for min 30 paired X-Y observations.
trigger: Post-C&E Matrix, before Correlation / Regression (#36)

name: DMAIC Correlation and Regression
procedure: a. Load paired X and Y data.
b. Pairwise correlation matrix; note |r| > 0.4.
c. Fit regression; escalate as diagnostics warrant.
d. Check R² (> 0.7), p-values (< 0.05), residual plots.
e. Identify vital few X's.
f. Document model and leverage points.
g. Feed vital X's into FMEA (#37).
trigger: Input DCP data collected (min 30 paired observations)

name: DMAIC Failure Modes Effects Analysis
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Process Improvement Backlog
procedure: a. Aggregate improvement candidates from FMEA, Quick Wins pending, VOC gaps, retro actions.
b. For each: name, one-sentence description, Day-2-Done criteria, effort, impact.
c. Score priority (RICE / WSJF / Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort).
d. Publish prioritized list to Sprint Planning.
e. Carry unfinished items forward.
trigger: Post-FMEA or at each sprint boundary

name: DMAIC Financial Benefit Translator
procedure: a. Identify benefit categories: hard-dollar, revenue lift, quality/rework, risk avoidance.
b. Quantify current cost / loss per period at baseline.
c. Project post-improvement cost / loss at target.
d. Compute annualized net benefit = 12 × monthly delta.
e. Apply confidence rating: Hard / Soft / Cost Avoidance.
f. Obtain Finance-partner sign-off.
g. Register in portfolio benefits ledger.
trigger: Baseline complete (projection) OR post-improvement (actual)

name: DMAIC Implemented Improvements
procedure: 1. Open Current Failure Modes Effect Analysis spreadsheet
2. Review each recommended action for improvement of process inputs
3. Identify Improvement Backlog Item(s)
4. Document Improvement Backlog Item(s) Name, Description, and Day 2 Done Criteria
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Project Results Narrative Document
procedure: a. Executive summary: problem → result → annualized benefit.
b. Background: business case, scope, goal.
c. Results: baseline vs remeasured, Control Chart before/after.
d. Root cause findings: vital X's, FMEA failure modes addressed.
e. Implemented improvements with before/after.
f. Financial benefit with confidence.
g. Control plan: ongoing monitoring, SOPs, Process Owner.
h. Lessons learned.
i. Review with Sponsor and file in portfolio.
trigger: Control phase complete, Financial Benefit signed off

name: Kaizen Project Charter
procedure: a. State problem in one paragraph with scope and pain observed.
b. Document business case.
c. Define event scope.
d. Set goal statement: baseline X → target Y by event end + 30 days.
e. Identify event team: Lead, Process Owner, SMEs, Sponsor.
f. Schedule event window.
g. Identify top 3 risks.
h. Obtain Sponsor signature.
trigger: Kaizen candidate approved for event

name: Kaizen Output Data Collection Plan
procedure: a. List the 1–3 CTQ output metrics from the Kaizen Charter goal.
b. For each metric document: operational definition, method, pre/post sampling plan, owner, tool.
c. If measurement is subjective, run a quick 3-appraiser MSA on 5 samples.
d. Execute pre-event collection on Day 1.
e. Schedule post-event collection at event end + 30 days.
f. Store DCP alongside Charter.
trigger: Event start

name: Kaizen Event Scheduling
procedure: 1. Review the Desired Project Team Roles on Project Charter
2. Select high performing subject matter experts to meet requirements of the team roles
3. Identify general timeframe of window of opportunity and negotiate availability and commitment
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event SIPOC
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event Prioritized Inputs
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event Failure Modes Effects Analysis
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Implemented Improvements
procedure: 1. Open Current Failure Modes Effect Analysis spreadsheet
2. Review each recommended action for improvement of process inputs
3. Identify Improvement Backlog Item(s)
4. Document Improvement Backlog Item(s) Name, Description, and Day 2 Done Criteria
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen project Results Narrative 3 Pager
procedure: a. Page 1 — Problem & Goal: statement, baseline, goal, team, dates, owner.
b. Page 2 — What Was Done: improvements, before/after diagrams, C&E/FMEA insights.
c. Page 3 — Results: remeasured metric, delta, secondary metrics, financial benefit, lessons.
d. Publish to Kaizen portfolio.
trigger: Post-remeasurement (event + 30 days)

name: Kaizen Process Owner Transition
procedure: a. Walk Process Owner through each implemented improvement and its performance vs baseline.
b. Confirm control measures: updated SOP, Control Chart thresholds, rollback plan.
c. Transfer ownership of ongoing monitoring.
d. Schedule 30/60/90-day Process Owner check-ins.
e. Both parties sign; file with Kaizen record.
f. Kaizen Lead steps back.
trigger: Kaizen Results Narrative complete AND remeasured metric captured

name: Quarterly Planning
trigger: First working day of each quarter
procedure: a. Review prior quarter: OKR confidence vs actual, Kaizens closed with validated benefit, sprint-goal completion rate.
b. Align to org priorities and externally imposed constraints for the coming quarter.
c. Draft quarterly OKRs (3–5).
d. Lay out 6 sprints + 1 reset sprint (Sprint 7) on the calendar.
e. Allocate Kaizen portfolio across sprints.
f. Identify Sprint 7 reset scope.
g. Publish to team, schedule Sprint 1 Planning.

name: Sprint Planning
trigger: Mon Wk1 of sprint, 09:30 local
procedure: a. Phase 1 (1h): Team selects Improvement Backlog items it commits to turning into fully documented improvements.
b. Phase 2 (1h): Team decomposes selected items into tasks with estimates and assignments.
c. Output: Sprint Backlog that reflects mutual commitment.

name: Daily Standup
trigger: Same time each work day, 09:00 local
procedure: a. Each member answers three questions: what have you done, what will you do next, what impedes you?
b. No side conversations; 15 minutes hard stop.
c. Post-standup side-meetings scheduled for interested parties.

name: Mid-Sprint Review
trigger: Fri Wk1 of sprint, 15:00 local
procedure: a. Team reviews sprint progress vs commitment.
b. Identify any items that should move out of sprint or be deferred.
c. Confirm plan for Wk2.

name: Sprint Review
trigger: Fri Wk2 of sprint, 14:00 local
procedure: a. Team presents sprint goal, committed backlog, completed backlog.
b. Members demonstrate completed improvements.
c. Stakeholders polled for feedback + priority changes.
d. Process Owner discusses backlog rearrangement.

name: Sprint Retrospective
trigger: Fri Wk2 of sprint, 15:00 local (immediately after Review)
procedure: a. Team answers: what went well; what could be improved?
b. Facilitator captures in summary form.
c. Prioritize improvements; add high-priority items to next sprint backlog.

name: Deep Work — Project Task (generic)
trigger: PROJECT bucket has slack and no DMAIC/Kaizen payload eligible
procedure: a. Declare intention for the block.
b. Work the primary project task uninterrupted.
c. At close, log output and any friction.

name: Value-Added Communication (generic)
trigger: COMMUNICATION bucket has slack and no named comm entry eligible
procedure: a. Triage inbox / chat / calendar for value-added touchpoints.
b. Respond deliberately (not reactively).
c. Log a short outcome note at close.

name: End-of-Activity Reflection
trigger: Close-of-day reflection anchor, 17:00 local
procedure: a. Scan the day's closed activities.
b. Note what went well.
c. Note what to improve.
d. Flag any friction signals for the Kaizen queue.

name: Weekly Reflection
trigger: Friday afternoon, 16:30 local
procedure: a. Define: what was the dominant pain pattern this week?
b. Measure: baseline rough count or duration.
c. Analyze: candidate causes.
d. Improve: promote at most one candidate to a Kaizen.

name: Lessons Learned
trigger: Every Kaizen close (every projectType, every closeKind)
procedure: a. What worked — improvements that beat baseline.
b. What didn't — improvements abandoned or reverted.
c. Next to try — hypotheses for the next iteration.
d. Publish alongside the Kaizen record.
